title: IBP — Last Public Insulation Installer After QXO/TopBuild Take-Private
summary: QXO's $17B take-private of TopBuild removes the #1 public insulation installer, leaving IBP as the sole large-cap pure-play. Q2 2026 beat (adj EPS $2.91 vs $2.55 est) validated the diversification thesis and reinforces the roll-up cadence.
catalyst: QXO/TopBuild deal announced April 19, 2026 (expected close Q3 2026) removes IBP's only large-cap public peer. Q2 2026 (Aug 6) delivered a beat: revenue $777.8M vs $743.96M consensus (record Q2), adj EPS $2.91 vs $2.55, with heavy commercial +15% offsetting new residential -6%. Insider cluster (CFO Miller, COO, Director) bought ~$1M in trailing three months with zero selling. Management reaffirmed $100M annual acquired-revenue cadence and raised the dividend to $0.39.
thesis: When a major public comparable goes private at a strategic premium, scarcity value typically re-rates the surviving public peer. IBP is now the only large-cap pure-play public exposure to residential and commercial insulation installation in North America — a vertical undergoing aggressive roll-up. The insider cluster suggests management sees either takeout optionality or that the post-deal scarcity premium is unpriced. Diversification (heavy commercial, manufacturing, distribution) is working: it more than offset the residential softness in Q2, meaning IBP's earnings power decouples from single-thread housing-starts data. Different mechanism from the berkshire-homebuilder-revaluation opp (builder multiple expansion) — this is an installer-scarcity / strategic-optionality play.
counter_thesis: Residential housing starts remain the largest single revenue driver; if new-construction weakness persists into 2027, the diversification math gets harder to grow the base. Strategic-buyer optionality is speculative — QXO already spent its firepower on TopBuild and has integration risk to work through before another deal. Insulation installation is labor-intensive and inflation-exposed; margin compression from wage pressure could dominate any consolidation premium. IBP has already re-rated ~9% since the cluster buys, so much of the easy scarcity premium may already be priced. Finally, valuation is not cheap — 19.5x forward P/E puts IBP above its historical median at a point in the housing cycle where earnings estimates could still be revised down.

ticker_rationale.IBP: Sole large-cap ($6B+) publicly-traded pure-play insulation installer post-TopBuild take-private. Q2 2026 record revenue + EPS beat + heavy-commercial acceleration + insider cluster + roll-up cadence all align. Currently trades at 19.5x forward P/E vs. TopBuild's take-private multiple of ~13x EV/EBITDA (a floor for what a strategic would pay if optionality materializes).

trade_construction.entry_zone: IBP $220-$235 (current $238; would prefer accumulation on pullback but $235 acceptable if Q3 preview stays constructive)
trade_construction.target_12mo: IBP $290 (+22% from $238) — 22x forward P/E on FY27E $13.20 EPS, or scarcity-premium re-rating to 21x on FY26 EPS
trade_construction.stop_loss: IBP $195 (-18% from $238) — closes below the pre-Q2-print consolidation and pre-QXO-deal level; would signal residential-cycle deterioration overwhelming diversification

confidence_note: Trade construction is best-available estimate. Would firm to High Conviction on any of: (a) second strategic acquirer (Beacon, ABC Supply, Builders FirstSource) signaling installer-sector interest with a bid or 13D filing; (b) IBP disclosing an M&A print >$50M single deal or annual acquired revenue trending >$120M; (c) Q3 2026 print confirming heavy-commercial growth accelerating to >20% YoY. Entry zone assumes no macro shock to housing before an entry decision is made.

catalyst_calendar.event: Q3 2026 earnings — check heavy-commercial growth, roll-up cadence, and any takeover-language in prepared remarks
Expected QXO/TopBuild close (announced April 2026, Q3 close target) — resolves the peer take-out and cements IBP's public-scarcity status

risks: Residential housing starts (largest revenue driver) remain weak or worsen through 2027
Wage inflation compresses installer margins faster than pricing power can absorb
QXO/TopBuild integration proves messy, cooling the M&A cadence hypothesis
Valuation (19.5x fwd P/E) leaves little cushion if earnings estimates get revised lower
IBP over-pays for a tuck-in acquisition, destroying multiple

invalidation.trigger: Q3 2026 heavy-commercial revenue growth reverts to flat or negative YoY
Two consecutive quarters of consolidated organic revenue declining >3% YoY
Insider cluster reverses — net insider selling exceeds $1M open-market in any single quarter
IBP announces a >$500M leveraged acquisition (leverage/execution risk breaks the thesis)
